log.entry: Presentation built from these tables: reports/Glymph_overview_dark.pptx (code/deck/). All gates pass: text fit with the real fonts, naming and punctuation, package and animation checks, the PowerPoint schema validator.

All 216 Glymph outputs present after the reruns; every library scored for every tool; tables collected (59744539, 59744540). Scaling with the frozen 0.3.1: 20,000 cells 3 min 26 s, 40,000 cells 4 min 56 s, 80,000 cells 7 min 31 s, 160,000 cells 13 min 42 s with 47.9 GB RAM and 18.6 GB GPU memory.

Resource tests repeated with the frozen 0.3.1 (throughput on one 4-GPU node, CPU only on three libraries, scaling at 20,000 to 160,000 cells), so the presentation and tables quote one version throughout. CellBender's scaling runs are reused.

Confirmation set at the default budgets, from the first scoring pass (all 12 libraries had finished; 0.3.1, then 0.3.0, then CellBender 0.3.2). All 12: cross-species removal 88.0%, 82.7%, 83.6% (0.3.1 above CellBender on 7); per-cell error 0.0217, 0.0183, 0.0433 (0.3.1 below CellBender on 10); rank agreement 0.65, 0.58, 0.54 (above CellBender on 10). Seven 10x cell-line mixtures: removal 92.5%, 91.5%, 92.6%; same-species counts kept 98.93%, 98.97%, 98.74%; error 0.010, 0.011, 0.041; rank 0.78, 0.74, 0.63. BD mix 2: removal 91.6%, 86.6%, 93.0%; error 0.011, 0.014, 0.044; rank 0.87, 0.68, 0.60. Four xenografts: removal 79.2%, 66.2%, 65.4%, but 0.3.1 keeps 97.3% of same-species counts against 99.3% and removes twice the expected same-species background (native loss 0.4 to 2.1%); error 0.045, 0.033, 0.046, worse than both on xeno_HSC_2 and xeno_noHSC_3. So on xenografts 0.3.1 removes more contamination and also too many of the cells' own counts: the level estimate there rests on one to five tested genes.

102 of 216 Glymph tasks stopped at the GPU check: the GPU Slurm handed out on hpc3-gpu-18-04 was already filled by another process, and because the check fails fast the node kept receiving tasks. None is a Glymph error. Resubmitted with hpc3-gpu-18-03 and hpc3-gpu-18-04 excluded (59744535 to 59744538); scoring and collection run again afterwards.

Glymph 0.3.1 frozen: chunked memory paths, wider silent-gene set with doublet-like cells left out of the cluster sums, retry with fewer clusters, three clusterings with the middle estimate kept, doublet-like flag. Known limits carried into the benchmark: kidney_rep2 is over-cleaned (1.2 to 1.3 times the true background), libraries with only a few tested genes vary between runs (up to 8 points of removal on xeno_HSC_1), and three 10x mixtures stay below CellBender on removal at the default budget. Run on all 54 libraries: 20261117-0607_glymph-031-alltier.

Glymph 0.3.1 frozen and submitted on all 54 libraries at four budgets. The other tools are not rerun; their outputs from the first all-tier run are linked in, and Glymph 0.3.0 is scored beside 0.3.1 as glymph_030.

Fifth round scored. Sparing doublet-like cells does not reduce the over-cleaning of kidney_rep2 (removed over truth 1.28 with, 1.30 without) and loses removal where the most contaminated cells are flagged: BD mix 1 87.1% and 88.4% against 91.4% without, parse_hgmm_sub1 66% and 68% against 82%. Kidney marker leakage 86 to 88% against 89%. Decision: the default does not spare them; the flag is still written (glymph_doublet_like) and --spare-doublets turns sparing on. Three tasks of the not-spared run failed on hpc3-gpu-18-03, whose GPU was already filled by another user's process (21.5 of 24 GB); the job script now checks the GPU before starting.

Fifth round, to set one default: the same code with doublet-like cells spared from the exclusion constraint (two replicates) and not spared (one). kidney_rep2 is over-cleaned in round three (removed over truth 1.19 and 1.33; 1.13 in 0.3.0), which sparing should reduce.

Rounds three and four scored (two replicates each; 15 development mixtures; CellBender 0.3.2 in brackets). Round three: removal 89.3% and 88.9% (83.5%), per-cell error 0.0172 and 0.0161 (0.0401), rank agreement 0.68 (0.48); kidney error 0.089 and 0.091 (0.097), removed over truth 1.00, tubule markers removed from other cells 88% (83%). BD mix 1: 91.9% and 91.4% (92.8%). parse_hgmm_sub1: 89.7% and 87.3% (66.8%), now that it gets an estimate. Round four was worse on kidney (error 0.093, removed over truth 1.07 to 1.09): giving cells far above the fit their own multiplier over-removes, so that part is withdrawn. Spread between replicates: 1.2 points of removal on average, up to 8 points on xeno_HSC_1 (two clusters, one tested gene); the three clusterings do not cure that, because the cell embedding itself differs between runs.

Fourth round: a cell with more than five times the counts background explains on its silent genes, and more than 5% of its counts there, is treated as doublet-like: no exclusion constraint, trend multiplier, flagged in the output (glymph_doublet_like). Every other called cell keeps its own multiplier (the earlier rule gave outliers the trend value). Two replicates and a 1% budget run.
Third round: the silent-gene estimate is made on three clusterings of the same cells and the middle one is kept (calib_seeds). Two replicates of the same settings to measure run-to-run spread.

Second round scored (doublet-like cells out of the cluster sums). Kidney: tubule-marker counts removed from other cells 79.6% to 88.9% (CellBender 83.2%); cell-line removal up on every 10x mixture. But removed over truth on kidney rose from 0.96 to 1.02 (1.31 on rep2): doublets now lose the partner cell's genes, which the genotype truth counts as real. Also seen: the level estimate moves between two runs of the same code on thin libraries (parse_hgmm_sub1 had an estimate in round one and none in round two; cortex nuclei removed 30% in one and 35% in the other).
The 160,000-cell library runs too: 12 min 48 s, 48 GB RAM (CellBender: 4 h 29 min, 112 GB RAM).

Why removal stops at 90 to 96% on cell-line mixtures although every other-species gene should be silent: a few doublets in a cluster express those genes for real and lift the cluster sum above background, so the gene is not called silent for that cluster. Decision: Glymph 0.2.0 sets the swap fraction from that estimate after the first fit and retrains with it fixed. First scores: 89.8% mean removal (0.1.0: 81.8%), no native loss, 99.4% of same-species counts kept. It matches CellBender on three libraries (GEM-X 96.5 against 96.6, 12k 97.3 against 97.5, 6k 93.9 against 94.5) and trails on four.

Experiment results: longer training, no early stopping and smaller batches change nothing (about 79% on the 10k v3 library either way). Fixing the swap fraction at 2% gives 93 to 97% on six libraries with no native loss, and over-removes on the 1k library whose true fraction is about 0.35%. So the swap fraction is the lever, and it has to be estimated per library.

A label-free estimate works (code/benchmark/diag_exclusion.py, then src/glymph/exclusion.py): for a group of similar cells, (observed minus expected ambient) divided by (depth times the pool-average profile) is at least the swap fraction for every gene and piles up at it for genes the group does not express. Estimates: 0.29, 1.14, 2.14, 1.73, 2.69, 1.45 and 2.5% against regression truths of 0.31 to 0.42, 1.24 to 1.36, 1.93 to 2.24, 1.44 to 1.69, 1.90 to 2.26, 1.31 to 1.91 and 1.14 to 1.62%. It reads high on the GEM-X library.

Five training experiments submitted to find the remaining lever (59722867 to 59722871): no early stopping, four times more steps, swap fraction fixed at 2%, both together, and smaller batches. Glymph 0.1.0 (gene-budget output) on all seven libraries: 76 to 87% of cross-species counts removed, up from 63 to 79%, with more same-species counts kept and still no integrity violations. Decision: change the output rule instead. Glymph 0.1.0 removes each gene's expected background total from the entries where background is most probable (thinning.gene_budget), the same objective as CellBender's output step, solved by a closed-form water-filling plus a bisection. The model and training are unchanged from v0. Submitted on all seven libraries (59722588), with the per-entry mode estimator as a comparison (59722589).

The parsimony prior failed. With it the swap fraction fell further on every library instead of rising. A second diagnostic (code/benchmark/diag_shape.py) shows why: the background inside cells is a mix of soup-shaped and average-cell-shaped counts, as modelled, but its gene profile differs from both by about 0.08 nats per count, far above sampling noise. The network explains those counts better than the fixed profiles can, so the likelihood prefers it. The prior stays in the code as an option, off by default.

Decision: Glymph 0.1.0. The likelihood bounds the swap fraction from above (native expression cannot be negative) but not from below, so it now gets a parsimony prior that lets it rise until the data stop it, a hard cap of 10%, a short freeze at the start, and a faster learning rate for the two global scalars. v0 results are kept as glymph_v0.

Diagnosis of the under-removal (code/benchmark/diag_budget.py): regressing each cell's cross-species counts on its depth gives the true ambient level and true swap fraction. Glymph's ambient level matches the truth within about 30% on every library, but its swap fraction is 0.6 to 0.8% where the truth is 1.1 to 2.3%. The network explains the missing background as native expression.
